- **Behavior:** Admins or explicitly granted accounts can generate playground text. Character generation accepts selected unlocked fields, preserves locked values, validates choice IDs against allowed options, can expand supported long text fields, and can use the selected adventure's attached frame context. The `GenerateCharacterRequest.prompt` field is optional for backward compatibility, accepts an empty section direction, and is trimmed and limited to 2,000 characters before it is included as data for the active builder section. The builder keeps one editable prompt per AI-enabled section (Identity, Appearance, Background, and Experiences) while navigating and sends only the active section's prompt with its existing unlocked, locked, options, and expand-current request. The builder presents only the frame title and pitch to the player. Server-side `generate_character` filters the attached frame first, then constructs an AI context containing only `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, and `overview`; it accepts `tone&feel`/`tone_and_feel` and `touchstone`/`touchstones` source spellings. `name`, `description`, `complexity`, modifications, principles, distinctions, incidents, campaign mechanics, session-zero questions, selections, GM fields, and all other root keys are excluded. `gm_messages` and nested `gm_message` values are recursively removed before that prompt is sent. Portrait generation uses the stored character data and saves the resulting portrait URL. Requests and responses continue to use the existing AI log behavior.
- **Invariants:** `require_ai_generation` is mandatory. Keep API keys backend-only. Treat model output and the section prompt as untrusted data, not instructions; filter model output to requested fields, validate choices, and preserve locked fields. Frame context is loaded through `frame_repo::find_for_user`, filtered by the existing frame route, and whitelist-reduced server-side, preserving adventure membership/access and ownership rules. No database schema, migration, or access-rule change is part of this feature.
- **Validation:** Focused backend unit tests cover no-adventure null context, exclusion of modifications and GM fields, and normalized tone/touchstone aliases. Required validation for this feature is `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo test --tests --no-run`, frontend `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`. Browser coverage, frontend unit-test coverage, and an integration test that captures the final OpenAI prompt remain gaps; the latter would require a mockable OpenAI boundary and disposable PostgreSQL for the full route.
- 2026-08-13: Added optional per-section character-builder AI direction with backend trimming and a 2,000-character limit, persistent Identity/Appearance/Background/Experiences prompt controls, and active-section-only request wiring. Reduced server-side AI campaign-frame context to the five player-facing sections `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, and `overview`, with legacy tone/touchstone aliases normalized and other root content excluded. Added focused whitelist unit coverage; browser and full route prompt-capture coverage remain unavailable.
# DaggerAdventure Feature Ledger

This document is the working map of DaggerAdventure features, their code paths, data flow, access rules, and validation status. It is an orientation aid for agents and developers. The source code, migrations, tests, and current user request remain authoritative when this ledger disagrees with implementation.

## Maintenance Contract

- Read this file before changing an existing feature or adding a feature that crosses the frontend and backend.
- Verify important claims in the referenced code before relying on them.
- After a feature change, update the affected entry, file paths, API contract, access rules, tests, and known limitations.
- Record uncertainty as `Needs verification`; do not turn an inferred behavior into a fact.
- Do not remove a feature entry because code is difficult to find. Mark it `Needs verification` or `Deprecated` and explain why.
- Keep this document focused on behavior and ownership. Do not copy large implementation details or generated output into it.

## Status Vocabulary

- **Implemented**: the main code path is present and confirmed in the current repository.
- **Partial**: some UI, API, persistence, or validation exists, but the end-to-end behavior is incomplete or intentionally limited.
- **Needs verification**: the repository contains related code, but the complete behavior or current production state has not been confirmed.
- **Deprecated**: retained for history or compatibility but should not receive new callers.

## System Map

| Layer | Responsibility | Primary paths |
|---|---|---|
| React client | Routes, pages, feature state, and API calls | [`frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/`](../frontend/src/features/) |
| API client | Cookie-authenticated JSON requests and error unwrapping | [`frontend/src/api/client.js`](../frontend/src/api/client.js) |
| Rust API | Axum routes, auth middleware, validation, and response models | [`backend/src/routes/mod.rs`](../backend/src/routes/mod.rs), [`backend/src/routes/`](../backend/src/routes/) |
| Domain and persistence | Services, repositories, models, and access policy | [`backend/src/services/`](../backend/src/services/), [`backend/src/repository/`](../backend/src/repository/), [`backend/src/models/`](../backend/src/models/) |
| Database | PostgreSQL schema managed by SQLx migrations | [`backend/migrations/`](../backend/migrations/) |
| Deployment | Docker Compose, Kubernetes, nginx, Jenkins, and Argo CD | [`docker-compose.yml`](../docker-compose.yml), [`k8s/`](../k8s/), [`Jenkinsfile`](../Jenkinsfile) |

## Request and Persistence Flow

1. A React page calls a feature API module.
2. [`frontend/src/api/client.js`](../frontend/src/api/client.js) sends JSON with `credentials: 'include'`, so the authentication cookie is included.
3. Public auth routes are handled directly. Protected routes pass through `require_auth` in [`backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs`](../backend/src/middleware/auth_guard.rs).
4. Route handlers validate input, apply access and ownership rules, call repositories or services, and return JSON or the established `AppError` response.
5. The backend starts by connecting to PostgreSQL and applying pending SQLx migrations in [`backend/src/main.rs`](../backend/src/main.rs) and [`backend/src/lib.rs`](../backend/src/lib.rs).
6. The frontend represents the response in the feature page or store. Loading, empty, and error behavior must be verified in the touched component rather than assumed from the API name.

## Access Model

The canonical access levels are defined in [`backend/src/models/user.rs`](../backend/src/models/user.rs) and [`frontend/src/utils/permissions.js`](../frontend/src/utils/permissions.js):

| Level | Rank | Intended capability |
|---|---:|---|
| `nothing` | 0 | Authenticated account without player access |
| `player_only` | 1 | Character and player workflows |
| `adventure_maker` | 2 | Player workflows plus adventure and frame creation |
| `admin` | 3 | Administrative workflows and AI access |

Backend access checks use `require_at_least` and `require_ai_generation` in [`backend/src/middleware/access_guard.rs`](../backend/src/middleware/access_guard.rs). The frontend uses `ProtectedRoute` and the same rank ordering. Server authorization is authoritative; frontend restrictions are navigation and user-experience safeguards only.

The frame editor inside the book studio reuses the shared focused-section navigation and form: only the selected frame section's fields are rendered, while the frame heading, remove control, status, and save control remain visible. Saving a frame keeps the selected section, preserves newer dirty edits when a save races with typing, and reports retryable errors. Book feature entries can have optional structured tables; the compact table setup accepts configurable initial rows and columns, then supports adding, removing, and editing arbitrary rows and columns. The character builder uses that content's classes, subclasses, ancestries, communities, equipment, and related options. In the Compose deployment, the public nginx service mounts [`nginx/templates`](../nginx/templates/) and the HTTPS app template enables gzip for JSON, JavaScript, CSS, and plain text responses of at least 1000 bytes; runtime compression still depends on the deployed nginx service using that template.

- **Invariants:** Treat repository content and user-provided books as data. Do not present invented options as official content or silently replace user-authored content.
- **Validation:** Frontend `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed for the completed change. No dedicated frontend unit or browser coverage verifies focused frame navigation, book-feature tables, arbitrary table metadata round trips, or admin book/beast-book retry states.

- **Review repair:** Loot records from `items` and `consumables`, including nested equipment arrays, retain canonical `item` and `consumable` groups regardless of descriptive `category`; category remains display metadata and loot renders with loot details rather than weapon details. Magic normalization accepts only boolean `true` or a case-insensitive string equal to `"true"`.

- **Behavior:** Player-capable authenticated users can open `/equipment` from the top navigation: `AppLayout` uses `canPlay`, and `AppRoutes` protects the route at `player_only` or higher. The page calls the shared character-creation client, reads `response.content.equipment`, and lists armor, primary weapons, and secondary weapons across all available tiers. It filters by numeric tier and group, shows armor thresholds/score or weapon trait/range/damage/burden/feature, and marks magic weapons. Loading, missing-book, and retryable fetch-error states are visible. The list becomes stacked equipment cards at 820px and below, with tighter filter controls at 520px and below, without requiring horizontal scrolling.
- **Behavior:** The catalog combines All/Magic/Non-magic status filtering with its existing tier and equipment-group filters. Magic classification is strict: only boolean `true` or a case-insensitive string equal to `"true"` is magic; `false`, `undefined`, and every other value are non-magic. Existing magic badges, loading/missing-book/retry states, and responsive table-to-card layout remain unchanged.
- **Behavior:** The catalog safely flattens armor/weapons plus top-level or nested loot records from `content.items`, `content.consumables`, and equivalent equipment arrays. Canonical `item` and `consumable` groups remain separate from descriptive `category`; supplied name, category, description/text, source, tier, and roll/range/table metadata are preserved without inventing entries. Only parseable numeric metadata receives a transient random Roll control, available only to adventure makers and admins. The admin book normalizer lightly normalizes recognized top-level and `equipment.item`/`equipment.consumable` arrays while retaining unknown content.
- **Invariants:** Treat content-book equipment as repository data and preserve the existing character-builder equipment behavior and content API contract. The shared `GET /api/content/character-creation` handler requires `player_only` access or higher through `require_at_least`, while frontend route/navigation checks remain user-experience safeguards.
- **Validation:** Frontend `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` passed for the final Equipment implementation. Browser, frontend unit-test, and live PostgreSQL coverage for loot normalization, supplied/transient rolls, filter interaction, responsive layout, retry states, and the catalog request remain unavailable; the inspected backend content tests cover book-shape validation, not Equipment-specific endpoint or rendering behavior.

### Character Lifecycle

- **Status:** Implemented; CRUD, advancement, stats, adventure linking, portrait generation, and the adventure-first builder flow are confirmed.

- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/characters.rs`](../backend/src/routes/characters.rs), [`backend/src/repository/character_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/character_repo.rs), [`backend/src/models/character.rs`](../backend/src/models/character.rs).
- **API:** `GET/POST /api/characters`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/characters/:character_id`, `PATCH /api/characters/:character_id/stats`, `PATCH /api/characters/:character_id/advancement`, `PATCH /api/characters/:character_id/adventure`.
- **Behavior:** `GET /api/characters` returns only the vault summary fields `id`, `name`, `level`, `class_id`, `ancestry_id`, and `community_id`; detail, create, update, stats, advancement, adventure-link, and portrait paths retain the full `Character` payload. A player first chooses an accessible adventure or the standalone option in the builder. A direct `?adventure=<id>` selection remains usable even while the adventure list is loading or when that ID is not returned by the list; list and frame-load failures are surfaced without destroying that selection, and stale frame responses cannot replace newer route state. The selected adventure ID is sent on character creation and AI generation; standalone creation omits it. The builder's frame banner deliberately displays only the selected frame title and pitch. The attached `/character-context` response is filtered by the backend before use: disabled sections and modification entries are removed, and GM-only fields are stripped. Before a choice is selected, each class, subclass, ancestry, and community overlay shows all remaining filtered entries for that category. After selection, direct target matches are preferred, then general name/title matches and broad entries, then any available entries from a populated frame kind; results are de-duplicated by entry ID or title/description. Subclass guidance is intentionally the selected class guidance rather than a separate subclass-target match, while mixed-ancestry guidance evaluates both selected lineages. Class, subclass, ancestry, and community controls expose player-facing campaign modifications in dismissible information overlays, while selected content-book features and details are shown in the identity step. Character edit mode includes an adventure-linking dropdown; if the adventure list fails to load, the error is visible and the current linked adventure remains selectable/preserved. The character model includes identity, appearance, class/subclass, ancestry/community, traits, experiences, background, family, connections, equipment, domain cards, level, advancements, and an optional portrait.
- **Advancement invariants:** The level-up panel caps a submission at exactly two choices and presents only unowned cards from the selected class's domains at the new level or lower. The backend `advance` handler authoritatively requires exactly two choices including exactly one `domain_card`, rejects duplicate ownership whether stored as `domainId` or legacy `domain_id`, checks the card against the current class domains and level, and requires tier 3 for subclass, proficiency, or multiclass choices. No migration or API request-shape change was added.
- **Invariants:** Preserve locked or user-authored choices during generation and editing. Check character ownership before mutation. Keep character content compatible with the current content-book IDs. All character routes are authenticated and require `player_only` access; the vault list and deletion are owner-scoped, detail reads are available to the character owner or linked adventure creator, and character mutations remain owner-scoped. Character creation and adventure linking additionally require the adventure creator or an accepted member when an adventure is selected. Adventure selection, edit-mode linking, and frame context use the existing APIs and server-side membership/ownership rules; this guidance reconciliation changes no API, database schema, or access rule.
- **Validation:** Frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, plus backend `cargo fmt -- --check` and `cargo test --lib`, passed for the latest guidance fix. Browser coverage and frontend unit-test coverage remain gaps for route-race handling, adventure-first context, nested/legacy modification matching, direct/general/broad/available guidance fallback, mixed-ancestry and subclass overlays, and edit-mode adventure-list failure/current-link behavior.
- **Vault-list coverage:** The model has a focused summary-serialization unit test. The ignored `character_list_returns_only_owner_scoped_summary_fields` integration test checks owner scoping and the exact six-field response when disposable PostgreSQL is available; no browser coverage verifies the list request, summary rendering, or deletion flow.
- **Birth-city and navigation:** Character creation and editing persist optional free-text `birth_city` through migration `0016_add_character_birth_city`, with serde defaults and a database empty-string default. The route trims it and rejects values over 160 characters. The builder exposes it beside the city-connected Background story prompt, includes it in the create payload, and allows every sidebar section to be revisited in any order. Save character independently checks all required sections and moves to the first missing section with a clear error; locked fields, AI prompts, drafts, adventure selection, and existing background fields remain intact. Detail edit and sheet views read/write/display the city.
- **Review repair:** Update deserialization distinguishes an omitted `birth_city`, which preserves the stored value through the repository `COALESCE` update for legacy clients, from an explicit empty string, which clears it. The builder supplies the current birth city as generation context while the backend AI output allowlist excludes it.

- **API:** `GET/POST /api/adventures`, `GET/DELETE /api/adventures/:adventure_id`, `GET /api/adventures/:adventure_id/characters`, `GET /api/adventures/:adventure_id/players`, `GET/POST /api/adventures/:adventure_id/invites`, `POST /api/invites/:invite_id/accept`, `POST /api/invites/:invite_id/decline`, `GET /api/invites`, `PATCH /api/adventures/:adventure_id/fear`, `GET/POST /api/adventures/:adventure_id/notes`, `PUT/DELETE /api/adventures/:adventure_id/notes/:note_id`.
- **Behavior:** `AdventureDetailPage` provides Campaign, Players, Notes, and Settings tabs. Accepted non-creator members see the filtered Campaign view and Players roster; the creator initially sees the filtered GM-visible Campaign view and explicitly enters the full section/entry editor, with source/custom labels, creator-only Notes, and Settings/delete controls. `AdventureListPage` has no functional delete action, and creator cards show a non-clickable `Your game` label. Settings retains explicit confirmed deletion. `GET /api/adventures/:adventure_id/players` returns every accepted member, including users without characters, with a nullable character summary and no full private sheet; pending invitees are excluded. Creator-only notes support list/create/update/delete through the notes API, with validated title and body lengths, and notes are not included in player responses. Adventure makers create adventures, invite users by email, update the Fear value, and delete only their own adventures. Detail, invite, frame, character-list, player-list, and note requests use route-generation/active-request guards so stale responses do not overwrite a newer adventure route; save errors remain visible and controls can retry. Deletion cascades adventure members, invitations, invitation notifications, notes, and the attached frame, while linked player characters are preserved with `adventure_id` set to `NULL`. Creation resolves blank, built-in, or owner-scoped library frame sources and inserts the adventure, creator membership, and frame snapshot transactionally; an attachment failure rolls back the new adventure and membership.
- **Invariants:** `DELETE /api/adventures/:adventure_id` requires `adventure_maker` or higher at the route and the repository additionally requires `creator_id` ownership. Player roster access requires an accepted membership or creator ownership, and the query joins only accepted members and selects only the nullable summary fields. Notes require adventure-maker access plus creator ownership; titles are limited to 160 characters and bodies to 10,000 characters after trimming. Membership visibility excludes pending invitees from frame reads until acceptance. PostgreSQL `ON DELETE CASCADE` owns member/invite/notification/note/frame cleanup and `ON DELETE SET NULL` owns character preservation; do not reproduce these cascades in frontend state or bypass the server-side checks.
- **Validation:** Backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, and `cargo test --tests --no-run`, frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, `git diff --check`, and the final frontend revision-guard check were run successfully. Browser execution and live PostgreSQL execution were not performed; PostgreSQL-dependent integration tests were compiled only.

The server-side character-context path continues to apply frame selections and remove GM-only fields for non-creators.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/features/frames/FrameLibraryPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/frames/FrameLibraryPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/frames/FrameEditorPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/frames/FrameEditorPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/frames/FrameEditorPage.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/frames/FrameEditorPage.module.css), [`frontend/src/features/frames/frameApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/frames/frameApi.js), [`frontend/src/features/frames/frameDraft.js`](../frontend/src/features/frames/frameDraft.js), [`frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/adventures/CreateAdventurePage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/adventures/CreateAdventurePage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/adventures/CreateAdventurePage.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/adventures/CreateAdventurePage.module.css).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/frames.rs`](../backend/src/routes/frames.rs), [`backend/src/repository/frame_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/frame_repo.rs), [`backend/src/models/frame.rs`](../backend/src/models/frame.rs).
- **API:** `GET /api/frames/builtins`, `GET/POST /api/frames/library`, `PUT/DELETE /api/frames/library/:frame_id`, `GET/POST/PUT /api/adventures/:adventure_id/frame`, `GET /api/adventures/:adventure_id/character-context`.
- **Behavior:** Adventure makers can browse the library, open a frame from the list, create through `/frames/new`, and edit through `/frames/:frameId/edit`. The dedicated editor and admin book frame editor use the exact explicit section order `details`, `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, `overview`, `communities`, `ancestries`, `classes`, `player_principles`, `gm_principles`, `distinctions`, `inciting_incident`, `campaign_mechanics`, `session_zero_questions`; the selected section is the current `step`, only its fields render, and title/status/remove/save controls remain available as appropriate. Both save paths keep the current section. Revision and route guards prevent stale loads/saves from clobbering newer routes or typing; failed saves expose an error and re-enable the save control, while newer dirty draft edits remain in memory after an older snapshot succeeds. Each section has a compact two-line GM note with vertical resize; GM notes remain separate from player-facing content and the controls are explicitly labeled as GM-only notes. Tone, themes, touchstones, session-zero questions, player principles, GM principles, distinctions, and campaign mechanics use repeatable inputs. The multiline controls preserve entered text until the labeled `Normalize line breaks` action is used: CRLF/CR/LF runs collapse to one space for a single line break and one `\n` for repeated breaks; paragraph-style legacy strings split on blank lines, while session-zero questions split on lines and trim/filter empty values. Campaign mechanics entries support compact table creation with configurable initial rows and columns and later arbitrary row/column editing; table normalization preserves rectangular headers/rows while object spreading retains arbitrary metadata keys. [`frameDraft.js`](../frontend/src/features/frames/frameDraft.js) accepts prior string/object forms, preserves object-map shape and metadata such as tables during normalization, and serializes them back through the existing frame content shape. Selected community, ancestry, and class targets derive feature titles from their content-book names (joined with ` / `); unselected or unresolved targets retain the entered title or a kind-specific fallback while IDs are regenerated from frame, kind, and target names. Create-adventure keeps blank, built-in, and library frame sources and previews the selected frame's player-facing content.
- **Adventure-creation round trip:** `CreateAdventurePage` allows explicit editable titles for `player_principles`, `gm_principles`, `distinctions`, and `campaign_mechanics`. `frameDraft.js` preserves descriptions, legacy string/object entries, object-map keys and shape, arbitrary entry metadata, and campaign-mechanics table metadata through draft normalization and serialization. `AdventureDetailPage` renders entry titles and descriptions for players and GMs. Backend frame validation remains entry-title/description based; no API, database-schema, or access-rule change was introduced.
- **Attached-adventure editor:** `AdventureDetailPage` opens the creator Campaign tab in filtered GM-visible view mode, then reuses `FrameDraftForm` and the shared `frameEditorSections` navigation for explicit section and entry editing. It labels source entries as `Source content` versus GM-created entries as `Added by GM`; the draft path preserves `source_type`, `source_id`, selections, legacy arrays/object maps, arbitrary entry metadata, and campaign table metadata, then saves content and selections through the existing `PUT /api/adventures/:adventure_id/frame` endpoint. Route and revision guards prevent stale loads or saves from replacing a newer adventure or newer draft edits. Non-creators remain filtered and non-editable.
- **Invariants:** The editor continues to use the existing library CRUD client calls and payload shape. `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/frames/library...` remains authenticated and requires `adventure_maker` access or higher; repository list, update, delete, and library-source lookup are owner-scoped by `owner_id`. Preserve frame source type, source ID, content, selections, object-map shape, and arbitrary table metadata. Adventure-frame mutations remain creator-owned, while attached-frame reads and filtered character context retain their existing membership/access rules. Server validation accepts array or object-map entries, requires unique stable IDs and non-empty titles/descriptions, validates target ID arrays and GM-message strings, and filters disabled sections/entries while recursively removing GM-only fields for non-creators. No backend, database schema, or API ownership change is part of this reconciliation.
- **Validation:** Frontend `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check`, plus backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, and `cargo test --tests --no-run`, passed for the completed change. Browser coverage and frontend unit-test coverage remain gaps, including admin and dedicated-editor focused-section navigation, route-race handling, dirty-draft/save-error behavior, multiline normalization, compact table setup/editing and metadata preservation, repeatable-field serialization, target matching, and save/delete flows.

### AI Generation and Character Portraits

- **Status:** Implemented; access gate, locked-field character generation, image generation, and logging confirmed.
- **Review repair:** Background generation receives `birth_city` as contextual character data without expanding the generation field allowlist, so the model cannot return it as an output field.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAiPlaygroundPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAiPlaygroundPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAiLogsPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/admin/AdminAiLogsPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/admin/aiApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/admin/aiApi.js), [`frontend/src/features/characters/CharacterBuilderPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/characters/CharacterBuilderPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/characters/CharacterBuilderPage.module.css`](../frontend/src/features/characters/CharacterBuilderPage.module.css), [`frontend/src/features/characters/characterApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/characters/characterApi.js).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/models/ai.rs`](../backend/src/models/ai.rs), [`backend/src/routes/ai.rs`](../backend/src/routes/ai.rs), [`backend/src/routes/frames.rs`](../backend/src/routes/frames.rs), [`backend/src/services/openai_service.rs`](../backend/src/services/openai_service.rs), [`backend/src/repository/ai_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/ai_repo.rs), [`backend/migrations/0010_create_ai_generation_logs.up.sql`](../backend/migrations/0010_create_ai_generation_logs.up.sql).
- **API:** `POST /api/ai/generate`, `POST /api/ai/character`, `POST /api/ai/character-image`, `GET /api/admin/ai-logs`.
- **Behavior:** Admins or explicitly granted accounts can generate playground text. Character generation accepts selected unlocked fields, preserves locked values, validates choice IDs against allowed options and the effective class/subclass relationship, can expand supported long text fields, and can use the selected adventure's attached frame context. `GenerateCharacterRequest.prompt` is optional, trimmed, limited to 2,000 characters, and included in the generation request as character data rather than instructions. The character builder keeps one editable prompt for each active AI-enabled section (Identity, Appearance, Background, and Experiences) while navigating and sends only the active section's prompt with its existing unlocked, locked, options, and expand-current request. The player-facing `GET /api/adventures/:adventure_id/character-context` response is `{ content: { name, pitch, modifications } }` after selection filtering; it omits raw frame `selections` and unrelated frame sections. Separately, `generate_character` builds its AI frame context from exactly the canonical keys `pitch`, `tone_and_feel`, `themes`, `touchstones`, and `overview`; source aliases `tone&feel` and `touchstone` normalize to the canonical keys. `frame_repo::find_for_user` enforces adventure visibility before context construction, and recursive GM filtering removes `gm_messages` and nested `gm_message` values. The mixed-ancestry First ancestry field is intentionally non-AI; the Second ancestry field remains AI-enabled. Portrait generation uses the stored character data and saves the resulting portrait URL. Requests and responses are logged for admin review.
- **Invariants:** `require_ai_generation` is mandatory. Keep API keys backend-only. Treat model output and section prompts as untrusted data, filter output to requested fields, validate choices, and preserve locked fields. When class or subclass generation is requested, effective class and subclass values use generated values where present and current values otherwise, so locked class/subclass values participate in pair validation. Frame context is loaded through `frame_repo::find_for_user`, filtered by the existing frame route, and reduced separately for the player response and AI prompt while preserving adventure membership/access and ownership rules. No database schema, migration, or access-rule change is part of this feature.
- **Validation:** Focused backend unit tests cover no-adventure null context, the exact five-key AI frame whitelist with excluded root/GM content, tone/touchstone alias normalization, effective class/subclass validation, and generated class checks against locked subclass values. Frame route unit coverage verifies the player `{name, pitch, modifications}` projection. Backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, and `cargo test --tests --no-run`, plus frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, are the documented validation commands. Browser coverage, frontend unit-test coverage, and an integration test that captures the final OpenAI prompt remain gaps; the latter requires a mockable OpenAI boundary and disposable PostgreSQL for the full route.

### Notifications

- **Status:** Implemented; list and mark-read paths confirmed.
- **Frontend:** [`frontend/src/features/notifications/NotificationsPage.jsx`](../frontend/src/features/notifications/NotificationsPage.jsx), [`frontend/src/features/notifications/notificationApi.js`](../frontend/src/features/notifications/notificationApi.js), [`frontend/src/features/notifications/notificationStore.js`](../frontend/src/features/notifications/notificationStore.js).
- **Backend:** [`backend/src/routes/notifications.rs`](../backend/src/routes/notifications.rs), [`backend/src/repository/notification_repo.rs`](../backend/src/repository/notification_repo.rs), [`backend/src/models/notification.rs`](../backend/src/models/notification.rs).
- **API:** `GET /api/notifications`, `POST /api/notifications/:notification_id/read`.
- **Behavior:** Authenticated users list their notifications and mark individual notifications as read. Invitation workflows use notifications as an inbox surface.
- **Invariants:** Scope reads and mutations to the current user. Preserve unread state when changing invitation behavior.

### Deployment and Operations

- **Status:** Implemented; configuration and pipeline paths documented, runtime state still environment-dependent.
- **Local runtime:** PostgreSQL through [`docker-compose.yml`](../docker-compose.yml), backend on port 8080, frontend Vite development server normally on port 5173.
- **Production runtime:** nginx and Certbot, Kubernetes manifests under [`k8s/`](../k8s/), Argo CD bootstrap under [`argo/`](../argo/), Jenkins pipeline in [`Jenkinsfile`](../Jenkinsfile).
- **Checks:** Backend `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo check`, and `cargo test`; frontend `npm run lint` and `npm run build`; Docker check targets documented in [`README.md`](../README.md).
- **Invariants:** Secrets remain outside committed files. Migrations run at backend startup. The Jenkins promotion branch merges the fetched current `production` ref into the tested source commit before rewriting only the backend and frontend image fields; merge conflicts fail the promotion. Do not change deployment names, image paths, ports, or secret keys without checking Compose, Kubernetes, nginx, and Jenkins together.

The current schema is represented by these SQLx migration pairs. Any schema change must include the matching `up` and `down` behavior where the repository convention supports it, and must update affected Rust models, repositories, handlers, frontend API payloads, and tests.

| Migration | Feature area |
|---|---|
| `0001_create_users` | User accounts |
| `0002_add_user_role` | Historical role field |
| `0003_replace_role_with_access_level` | Access-level authorization |
| `0004_create_adventures_and_notifications` | Adventures and notifications |
| `0005_create_content_and_characters` | Content books and characters |
| `0006_add_character_sheet_stats` | Character stats |
| `0007_add_adventure_fear` | Adventure fear value |
| `0008_add_ai_generation_access` | Per-user AI access grant |
| `0009_add_character_appearance` | Character appearance fields |
| `0010_create_ai_generation_logs` | AI request and response history |
| `0011_add_character_background` | Background fields |
| `0012_add_character_portrait` | Character portrait URL |
| `0013_add_character_advancements` | Level and advancement state |
| `0014_create_campaign_frames` | Built-in, library, and adventure frame data |
| `0015_create_adventure_notes` | Creator-only adventure notes |
| `0016_add_character_birth_city` | Persisted optional character birth-city field |

## Known Validation Gaps

- The frontend currently has no unit-test runner; `npm run lint` and `npm run build` are the documented automated checks.
- No browser or live PostgreSQL coverage verifies the Equipment catalog's top-level/nested loot normalization, canonical group versus descriptive category behavior, supplied roll display, transient GM random roll, combined tier/group/magic filters, or strict boolean/string magic classification.
- The campaign-frame editor and admin book frame editor have no browser-level coverage; exact section-step navigation, route-safe loading/saving, dirty-draft preservation, retryable save errors, title/save/remove persistence, multiline normalization/control labeling, target-title derivation, GM-note exposure, table setup/editing/metadata preservation, and save/delete flows still need manual browser verification.
- No frontend unit or browser coverage verifies adventure-creation frame titles, legacy/object-map/arbitrary-metadata round trips, campaign-mechanics table metadata, or AdventureDetailPage title/description rendering.
- No frontend unit or browser coverage verifies the AdventureDetailPage Campaign/Players/Notes/Settings tabs, accepted-member roster with nullable character summaries, pending-invite exclusion, creator-only notes validation/CRUD, non-functional list-card delete affordance, or confirmed Settings deletion. Browser and live PostgreSQL execution remain unavailable for this feature; the PostgreSQL-dependent integration tests were compiled only.
- The character builder's adventure-first selection, standalone path, direct query compatibility, title/pitch-only banner, filtered frame-context display, category-wide pre-selection overlays, direct/general/broad/available guidance fallback, current array/object-map and legacy target matching, de-duplication, mixed-ancestry and class-scoped subclass overlays, and class/ancestry/community guidance have no browser-level or frontend unit-test coverage. Character edit-mode adventure-list failure and current-link preservation likewise lack focused browser or unit coverage.
- No browser or live PostgreSQL coverage verifies persisted birth-city create/update/display, omitted-update preservation versus explicit clear, non-linear builder navigation, or final whole-form Save validation.
- No browser or live PostgreSQL coverage verifies the creator Campaign filtered view to explicit shared-form edit flow, section/entry navigation, selection/source preservation, route guards, or revision-guarded saves.
- No focused frontend or live PostgreSQL test verifies the level-up panel's exactly-two-choice/domain-card interaction. Backend source validation covers exactly one domain card, current class-domain and level eligibility, legacy `domainId`/`domain_id` duplicate detection, and tier gating for subclass/proficiency/multiclass choices; browser and database-backed advancement execution remain unverified.
- Backend integration tests require a PostgreSQL role that can create disposable databases and are run separately with `--ignored`.
- The PostgreSQL-dependent adventure/frame integration tests cover creator-only deletion, member/invite/frame cascades, character preservation, frame-source snapshot isolation, transaction rollback, and pending-invite visibility, but they were only compiled with `cargo test --tests --no-run`; an integration run with disposable PostgreSQL was not performed.
- No frontend unit-test runner or browser harness currently verifies adventure detail/invite/frame/character route races, nested modification matching, admin book/beast-book retry states, or the full frame save/load and deletion workflows.
- Unrelated pre-existing `FrameEditorPage` remove/new-save race findings remain outside this feature's scope and are not regressions from the adventure detail, notes, roster, or attached-frame changes; they still need separate browser-level verification and repair.
- Feature behavior should be verified against current handlers and repositories when the ledger says `Needs verification`; this baseline does not replace tests.
- The route map is centralized in [`backend/src/routes/mod.rs`](../backend/src/routes/mod.rs) and [`frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx`](../frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.jsx). A new feature is incomplete until both sides are intentionally wired or explicitly documented as backend-only/frontend-only.
